questions.question: What is another name for frozen carbon dioxide?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Dry Ice.**__

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Frozen carbon dioxide** is commonly known as** dry ice.**
 
• It is called dry ice because it is **solid carbon dioxide and does not melt** but **sublimates directly from solid to gas.**
 
• Dry ice is used in various industries for** cooling purposes, such as transporting perishable goods, creating smoke and fog effects** in the entertainment industry, and cleaning surfaces.
 
• It is also used in the medical field for **cryotherapy, **which involves the freezing of tissues to remove abnormal growths.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Refrigerant** is a substance used in refrigeration systems to transfer heat and cool the environment. Frozen carbon dioxide is not commonly used as a refrigerant.
 
• **Coal** is a fossil fuel formed from the remains of ancient plants. It is not related to frozen carbon dioxide.
 
• **Coke** is a solid fuel made from coal. It is also not related to frozen carbon dioxide.

***Therefore, the correct answer is option 3, Dry Ice.***

questions.question: The space-filling model emphasises the relative size of each atom based on its ______.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**van der Waals radius**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• The space-filling model represents atoms as spheres with sizes proportional to their **van der Waals radii**.
 
• **Van der Waals radius** defines the effective size of an atom when it is not bonded to another atom, representing its physical boundary.
 
• In the space-filling model, overlapping spheres illustrate the physical arrangement of atoms in a molecule, showcasing their spatial proximity.
 
• This model is particularly useful for visualizing the overall shape, volume, and close-packing of molecules.
 
• It emphasizes the steric factors and spatial constraints, which are crucial in molecular interactions, such as protein-ligand binding or crystal packing.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Covalent Radius**: The covalent radius refers to half the distance between the nuclei of two identical atoms bonded covalently. It is smaller than the van der Waals radius since atoms are closer in bonded states.
 
• **Ionic Radius**: This is the effective radius of an ion in a crystal lattice. It depends on the ion's charge and coordination number, differing significantly from the van der Waals radius.
 
• **Van der Waals Forces**: Weak intermolecular forces arising from temporary dipoles in atoms or molecules. The van der Waals radius is a measure of the distance where these forces become significant.
 
• **Space-Filling Model Applications**: These models are widely used in structural biology and materials science to study molecular shape, packing, and steric hindrance.
 
• **Limitations of the Space-Filling Model**: Although visually intuitive, it may obscure detailed bonding information and is less effective for depicting smaller molecules or bond-specific interactions.

questions.question: Which of the following is NOT a property of graphite?

options.text: It is a conductor of electricity.
It has a lower density than diamond.
It is a conductor of heat.

questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**It has low melting point.**__

__** [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] Key Points__**

__
 
• Graphite is an allotrope of carbon.
 
• **It is a conductor of heat and electricity.**
 
• **It has a lower density than diamond.**
 
• Graphite is used as a lubricant in high temperatures.
 
• Because it has a high melting point.
 
• Hence statement 4 is the correct answer.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• In graphite single carbon atom is bonded with the other three carbon atoms.
 
• So it looks like a sheet in a three-dimensional figure.
 
• Between the sheets, weak forces are there.
 
• It has hexagonal rings of strongly bonded carbon atoms while weak interplate bonds.
 
• So it is a soft solid and uses as a lubricant.

questions.question: Which among the following is not an alkali metals and does not belong to the Group 1 of Periodic Table?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Calcium.**__ [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Calcium** is **not **an alkali metal and does not belong to Group 1 of the periodic table.
 
• **Alkali metals** are **highly reactive metals** that readily lose their outermost electron to form cations with a **charge of +1.**
 
• Any of the six chemical elements in Group 1 (Ia) of the periodic table—**lithium (Li), sodium (Na), potassium (K), rubidium (Rb), cesium (Cs), and francium (Fr)**—are classified as an alkali metal.
 
• The reason the alkali metals have that name is because they react with water to produce **alkalies,** which are **powerful bases **capable of **neutralizing acids.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Calcium:**

 
 
• It is an **alkaline earth metal **that belongs to **Group 2** of the periodic table.
 
• The elements in **Group 2** of the periodic table have **two valence electrons** and are **less reactive **than alkali metals. 
 
 
 
• **Lithium:**
 
 
• A chemical element with the **atomic number 3** and the symbol **Li **is lithium.
 
• It is a **delicate, white-silver alkali metal.**
 
• It is the **least dense metal** and the least dense solid element under typical conditions.
 
 
 
• **Sodium:**
 
 
• The chemical element sodium has the atomic number **11** and the symbol **Na.**
 
• It is a** delicate, silvery-white meta**l that is exceedingly** reactive.**
 
 
 
• **Potassium:**
 
 
• The chemical element with the atomic number **19 **and the letter** K** is potassium.
 
• It is a** silvery white metal **that may be easily sliced with a knife thanks to its pliability.

questions.question: Galvanisation is a process in which a protective ______ coating is applied on iron to prevent it from rusting.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Zinc**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• Galvanization is the process of applying a coating of zinc to steel or iron. 
 
• This is done to protect steel and iron from the process of rusting.
 
• The most common method of galvanization is " hot-dip-galvanization".
 
• In this method, parts are submerged in a bath of molten hot zinc.​

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• When zinc is coated on iron or steel, it protects corrosive substances from reaching the underlying steel or iron. 
 
• The electroplating such as chromate conversion coating is applied to provide further surface passivation to the substrate material.
 
• The hot-dipping method is not applicable to materials that are constantly exposed to acid and acid rains.
 
• It is also applicable to bolts and nuts.

questions.question: According to Newland's Law of Octaves, every eighth element has properties similar to those of the first element. Which of the following elements has properties similar to those of N?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**P**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Newlands' Law of Octaves:**

 
 
• John Newlands, an English chemist, proposed the Law of Octaves in 1865.
 
• He arranged the known elements in order of increasing atomic mass.
 
• He observed that every eighth element had properties similar to the first, much like the octaves in music.
 
• This law was an early attempt to find patterns in the properties of elements.
 
• The law was based on the atomic weights of the elements known at that time.
 
• The law was only applicable to elements up to calcium.
 
• Beyond calcium, the law failed because heavier elements did not follow the pattern.
 
• The periodic table was not fully developed at the time of Newlands.
 
• The later discovery of noble gases, also disrupted the octaves.
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Nitrogen (N) and Phosphorus (P):**

 
 
• Nitrogen and Phosphorus belong to Group 15 (also known as the Nitrogen group or pnictogens) of the periodic table.
 
• They have similar chemical properties due to their similar electron configurations.
 
• Both have five valence electrons, which are the electrons in the outermost shell.
 
• This similarity in valence electrons leads to similar bonding behavior.
 
• Both can form covalent bonds.
 
• Both can form compounds with similar formulas.
 
• Both can have multiple oxidation states.
 
• Both are non-metals.
 
• Nitrogen and phosphorus are essential elements for life.
 
• They both can form acids.
 
• They both can form oxides.

questions.question: The process in which metals are extracted from their ores by heating beyond the melting point is called __________.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Smelting**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Smelting** is a process in which metals are extracted from their ores by heating beyond their melting point. During this process, the metal is separated from its impurities and a pure form of metal is obtained.
 
• Smelting is commonly used for extracting metals such as iron, copper, lead, and zinc from their ores. It is an important process in the metallurgical industry.
 
• Spinning is a process of twisting fibers together to make yarn or thread. It is not related to the extraction of metals from their ores.
 
• Heaving is not a process used in the extraction of metals from their ores. It is a term used to describe the upward movement of soil or rocks due to frost or ice.
 
• Extracting is a general term used for any process of separating a substance from its mixture or compound. It can refer to the extraction of metals, oil, or any other substance.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• Smelting is a highly energy-intensive process and requires a high temperature to melt the metal. The process can produce a lot of air pollution and greenhouse gases.
 
• Spinning is a process commonly used in the textile industry to make fabrics and clothing. It involves twisting fibers together to create a yarn or thread, which is then woven into fabric.
 
• Heaving is a geological process that occurs due to the expansion of soil or rocks when they freeze. The expansion can cause the soil or rocks to move upward, which can lead to landslides or other geological hazards.
 
• Extracting can refer to the extraction of any substance from its mixture or compound. For example, oil can be extracted from the ground using drilling and pumping techniques.

questions.question: Which among the following is a cooking procedure in which the sugar in the food gets oxidized, turning into a brown colour?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Caramelisation.**__ [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Caramelisation** is a **cooking procedure** in which the sugar in the food **gets oxidized,** turning into a** brown colour.**
 
• This process involves** heating sugar** to a certain temperature, causing it to break down and form new compounds that give the food a** distinct flavour and colour. **
 
• Caramelisation is commonly used in **cooking and baking** to add flavour and colour to dishes such as** caramel sauce, crundefinedme brundefinedlundefinede, and caramelized onions.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Filtration:** a process of separating solid particles from a liquid by passing it through a** porous material **such as a **filter paper or mesh.**
 
• **Emulsification:** a process of **combining two immiscible liquids** such as oil and water to form a **stable mixture.**
 
• **Bromination:** a chemical reaction that involves the addition of **bromine to a compound,** often used in organic chemistry.
